cards.explanation: The answer is the area in front of the lampstand. The LORD says the seven lamps “…are to light the area in front of the lampstand.” Seven little flames, and every one of them points forward. Aaron does exactly that, setting them up facing toward the front, just as the LORD had commanded Moses (Numbers 8:3). I once got called out of a junk drawer for a job, so I know the feeling of being handed a clear assignment and wanting to get it right.

The answer is False. The text says Aaron did so, and he set up the lamps facing toward the front of the lampstand, “…just as the LORD had commanded Moses.” No remix, no creative twist, friends. He heard the instruction and he followed it.

The answer is Moses. The lampstand was fashioned “…according to the pattern the LORD had shown Moses.” The design didn't come from a craftsman's good idea, friends. The LORD showed the pattern to Moses, Israel's leader, and it got built that way.

The answer is to make them ceremonially clean. The LORD says, “Take the Levites from among the Israelites and make them ceremonially clean.” That comes before the bulls and before the presenting, bakers. Cleansing is the first step.

The answer is to shave their whole bodies and wash their clothes. After the sprinkling, the LORD says to “Have them shave their whole bodies and wash their clothes, and so purify themselves.” It's a head-to-toe fresh start, friends. The Levites do the work themselves, and I bet they felt very clean afterward.

The answer is True. The LORD tells Moses, “…you are to take a second young bull for a sin offering.” So there are two bulls in all, bakers. The first one comes with its grain offering, and this second one is for the sin offering.

The answer is True. The LORD says to “…present the Levites before the LORD and have the Israelites lay their hands upon them.” The whole congregation is assembled at the Tent of Meeting (Numbers 8:9), and the Israelites are the ones to lay hands on the Levites. The text doesn't say how it all happens, so I'll leave it right there.

The answer is so they can do the LORD's service. Aaron presents the Levites as a wave offering from the sons of Israel “…so that they may perform the service of the LORD.” That's the stated purpose, friends, so it's the one to hold on to. They're presented for service.

The answer is atonement. The Levites lay their hands on the heads of the bulls, and one is offered as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, “…to make atonement for the Levites.” Atonement is the whole point of those two bulls, bakers.

The answer is belong. The LORD says, “…you shall separate the Levites from the rest of the Israelites, and the Levites will belong to Me.” They're set apart, and they're His, friends. That's a pretty good thing to be.

The answer is False. No full year is mentioned anywhere here, bakers. The LORD says that after Moses has cleansed the Levites and presented them as a wave offering, “…they may come to serve at the Tent of Meeting.” Cleansed, presented, then they may serve.

The answer is the day He struck Egypt's firstborn. The LORD says every firstborn male in Israel is His, and “I set them apart for Myself on the day I struck down all the firstborn in the land of Egypt.” That's the day He set them apart, friends. Now He's taking the Levites in their place.

The answer is gift. The LORD says, “…I have given the Levites as a gift to Aaron and his sons from among the Israelites…” The word is gift, bakers. They were given to Aaron and his sons to perform the service.

The answer is so no plague comes on Israel near the sanctuary. The Levites serve and make atonement for the Israelites “…so that no plague will come against the Israelites when they approach the sanctuary.” That's the reason the LORD gives for it, friends. It's all about the Israelites approaching the sanctuary.

The answer is False. The text says the Levites came to perform their service at the Tent of Meeting “…in the presence of Aaron and his sons.” Moses is named in that verse too, but as the one the LORD commanded. The Levites serve in the presence of Aaron and his sons, and the elders aren't mentioned there. Think of it like a first day on the job where you're working right next to the people in charge (Numbers 8:22).
The answer is twenty-five. The LORD says, “Men twenty-five years of age or older shall enter to perform the service in the work at the Tent of Meeting.” Twenty-five is where the work begins, friends.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “…at the age of fifty, they must retire from performing the work and no longer serve.” Fifty is the line, bakers, and the verse says must. Now hold your hats, because retirement isn't the end of the story. Verse 26 says they “…may assist their brothers in fulfilling their duties at the Tent of Meeting, but they themselves are not to do the work” (Numbers 8:26).

The answer is assist. The LORD says that after that, “…they may assist their brothers in fulfilling their duties at the Tent of Meeting, but they themselves are not to do the work.” So he's still part of the team, friends. He just isn't doing the work himself.
